decision.title: WASI test runner disables V8 fast API calls

item.p: Problem: the xpath_parse test crashed Node.js (SIGSEGV, exit 139) about one run in eight on the wasm preset; deep_nesting_needs_no_recursion alone, after it had passed. Not a memory error in sxml: the same test is clean under ASan/UBSan (Clang, GCC) and valgrind, and the crash is not a wasm trap or a stack overflow (it happens with --stack-size=200 too).

Cause: in Node 22 the WASI imports are V8 fast API callbacks. fd_write allocates through uvwasi, which reports external memory to V8 and can start a full garbage collection inside the fast call; the collector then faults walking the optimized wasm frame (InnerPointerToCodeCache::GetCacheEntry). Whether a collection falls there depends on heap timing, hence one run in eight; tests that grow linear memory a lot (20,000 nested parentheses) make it likely. --no-allow-allocation-in-fast-api-call turns it into a deterministic V8 abort in WASI::FdWrite's FastCallback (45 of 60 runs).

Decision: tools/run-wasi.mjs sets --no-turbo-fast-api-calls through v8.setFlagsFromString before compiling the module, so WASI functions are called the ordinary way. 0 failures in 110 runs afterwards, also with allocation in fast calls forbidden. The test depth and the wasm stack size stay as they are; the library is not involved. Revisit when the runner's Node version no longer uses fast calls for WASI.
